newsitem.title: INDIA: New Indian government gets more support.
newsitem.headline: New Indian government gets more support.

text.p: Former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party said on Tuesday it would join Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's new centre-left government.
"The decision was taken in the interest of the nation and the stability of the government," party leader G.K. Moopanar told reporters in the southern city of Madras.

The TMC said on April 19 it had tentatively decided to stay out of Gujral's government after Moopanar was passed over by the ruling United Front coalition as its choice for new leader and prime minister.
"I congratulate Moopanar on the correct and wise decision taken," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told Reuters.

Indian shares surged in kerb trading after the decision was announced. Traders said the Bombay Stock Exchange's 30-share benchmark index was likely to jump by up to 50 points when the bourse reopened on Wednesday.

TMC leaders authorised Moopanar on Sunday to take a decision on behalf of the party, the third largest component in the 15-party United Front with 20 of the alliance's 178 deputies in the 545-member lower house of parliament.

Financial markets had been watching keenly to see if the TMC would return to the government because Chidambaram was expected to be asked to resume as finance minister and pilot the 1997/98 (April-March) budget through parliament, which reconvenes on Wednesday.
Chidambaram, who presented the budget in parliament on February 28, had proposed to slash income taxes, lower corporate taxes and reduce import tariffs.
The budget has been warmly welcomed by domestic industry and foreign investors.

Moopanar urged the Congress party, which gives make-or-break support to the ruling alliance in parliament, and some left-wing parties, which are part of the coalition but not in the government, to join Gujral's government as well.
"For greater stability of the United Front government, all parties supporting it from outside, including Congress and the Left, should participate in the government," Moopanar said.
